_what: Racquet and multi-purpose court surfaces at the Town Center, snapped from georeferenced aerial imagery.
_why_this_file_exists: Karen asked for 'Pickleball and Tennis'. town_center_buildings.json had already
flagged the courts as the one Town Center surface that could be fitted
automatically rather than read by a human, and left them out only because that
pass was about buildings. This is that follow-up.
_why_these_could_be_automatic_when_the_b: Court paint is the single Town Center surface with a colour signature of its own:
a court samples b-r = +65, against +18 to +28 for every roof and every stretch of
asphalt. Roofs and car parks are inseparable from each other by any threshold --
that is why the buildings had to be read by eye -- but the courts separate cleanly,
so these are thresholded and fitted with a minimum-area rectangle rather than
_how_measured: Same Google satellite frame used for the marina pad and the dog park. Its
georeference was re-solved for this pass rather than reused: the shot's water
mask was correlated against the reconciled pond and shoreline network over every
possible offset, and the scale was swept rather than assumed.
The sweep peaked at 1.2486 m/px -- independently reproducing the figure already
recorded in the README -- at 35.9 sigma above the correlation surface.
The fit was then verified the way this project requires: known pond outlines were
drawn back onto the shot and land on real ponds (19 of them in frame).
Each court blob was reduced to its minimum-area rectangle, which is the honest
shape for a court, and is expressed below in metres east/north of the same Town
_accuracy: +/-3 m, better than the buildings because the edges are machine-fitted rather than read by eye. Court 1 measures 77.4 x 41.2 m for four courts -- 19.3 m per court against a tennis court's 18.3 m with run-off -- and court 4 fits its rectangle at fill 1.01, both of which say the scale and the edges are right.
_naming: SETTLED. Minto's published amenity site plan labels the western bank 'Tennis' and
the eastern group 'Pickleball', with the 'Community Services Building' standing
between them. That split matches this geometry exactly: court 1 runs from -111 to
-34 m east, then there is a 38 m gap -- the building -- and then courts 2 and 3 run
from +4 to +87 m east with only 5 m between them. West of the gap is tennis, east of
The measurements agree independently. Court 1 is 77.4 x 41.2 m: four bays at 19.3 m
against 18.3 m for a tennis court with run-off, and 41.2 m deep against 36.6 m for a
tennis court's length with run-off. Courts 2 and 3 are the same overall depth but
divided far more finely, which is what a pickleball bank looks like.
Reading a NAME off Minto's plan is reference use and not derivative work -- the plan
is licensed for use as-is, and which sport is played on a court is a fact rather than
the artwork. No geometry came from it; every rectangle here is still machine-fitted
Court 4 is a single separate surface next to the fitness centre, confirmed by Karen
as the Multi-Purpose Court. It is named 'Multi-Purpose Court' and not 'Multi-Purpose
Court & Bocce' as the amenity list has it, because whether the bocce lanes are this
surface or a separate one next to it was not established -- and Minto's plan marks
'Bocce' as its own item some way west of here, which suggests they are separate.
_one_label_on_the_map: The three racquet banks still carry ONE combined map label, 'Pickleball & Tennis'.
That is now a layout decision rather than an admission of doubt: at community scale
the tennis and pickleball centroids are 115 m apart, which is a few millimetres on
the printed sheet, so two labels would collide and read worse than one true one.
The per-bank identification lives here in the data, where it is exact.
_dropped: A fifth blue blob 230 m east passed the colour test and was rejected: it sits
among houses on a residential street, is 21.8 x 19.2 m and nearly square, and
fits its rectangle at only 0.65. It is a private pool or a roof, not a court.
